label: a6-050-lem-cauchy-sequence-bounded
tail:
I have examined every step of the proof, all cited dependencies, and the remarks. The main proof is logically valid, uses the declared facts correctly, and contains no errors that affect the truth of the statement. I found one nonfatal defect in a remark.

### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, second bullet
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "the alternating sequence of [[fs-bounded-implies-convergent]] is bounded and, being divergent, is not Cauchy ([[lem-convergent-implies-cauchy]] would otherwise make it convergent by [[thm-cauchy-criterion-via-lub]])."
WHY IT FAILS: The parenthetical assigns to `lem-convergent-implies-cauchy` the role of making a Cauchy sequence convergent. That lemma (inferable from its title) states that every convergent sequence is Cauchy, not the converse. The intended reasoning is that if the sequence were Cauchy, `thm-cauchy-criterion-via-lub` would force it to converge, contradicting the claimed divergence. The citation of `lem-convergent-implies-cauchy` is either misplaced or misdescribed, rendering the sentence logically garbled. The surrounding mathematical point (bounded ≠ Cauchy) remains correct, so the defect is limited to this remark.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Replace the parenthetical with “if it were Cauchy, [[thm-cauchy-criterion-via-lub]] would make it convergent” or remove the confused citation.

0 fatal, 1 nonfatal
